taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): trees 60-150 dm, stems 1-3 (or 4).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): trees to 150 dm.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): trees.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: deciduous, the leaves turning orange and red in autumn.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): no prickles or thorns described.

traits.bark_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): bark grey to bronze; drawn grey; sRGB by eye.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves dull green to bluish green above, paler beneath; sRGB by eye.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves pinnately compound.

traits.division_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pinnately compound, leaflets opposite.

traits.division_order.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets undivided.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): the pinnate leaves end in a leaflet (odd-pinnate).

traits.leaflets.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 11-17 (to 19).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves 10 cm to 22 cm long.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets (2.5-)3-6 (to 7.5) cm long.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 1.5-2 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets oblong to oblong-lanceolate or oblanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet apex acute to obtuse.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins serrate at least on the outer half.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): panicles flat-topped or rounded, 6-18 cm across; drawn as a flat-topped corymb, as they read.

traits.inflorescence_outline.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flat-topped or rounded.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): panicles 75-200+-flowered.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the flat-topped panicle's 6 to 12 primary branches, each branching again to its flowers; FNA gives no count.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 6-18 cm across.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 8-11 mm across.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white, orbiculate, (3-)4-5 mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white; sRGB by eye.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 15-20.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes 8-12 mm across.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes yellow or orange-red to red; drawn orange-red; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes globose to subglobose.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering spring; read as May and June, as in northern Europe.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Sorbus aucuparia (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruiting fall; read as August to October.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a small upright tree of grey bark with ferny pinnate leaves, flat creamy flower heads and heavy clusters of orange-red berries.

allometry.note: 14.0 m tall at 30 years in the open, inside the floras' 6-15 m, as grown (2026-10-19). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
